articles.title: I spent a weekend with Gen Alpha. I needed a translator
articles.summary: From “huzz” to “unc” to “fries,” Gen Alpha has a growing vocabulary that can leave older generations confused. Here’s what their latest slang means.
articles.body:
As a youth mental health reporter , I'd like to think that I'm up to date with what young people are saying .

Then I spent a weekend volunteering with elementary, middle and high schoolers at a youth camp.

I heard "huzz," " larping " and "fries." One counselor was designated " unc ." When I watched kids throw up an OK-hand gesture and say "fairs," I had to stop to ask what all of these words meant.

Gen Alpha's slang can feel like an entirely different variant of the English language, shaped by TikTok, memes and Twitch streamers.

Here are some of the Gen Alpha slang terms you're likely to hear these days, and what they actually mean.

"Fairs" is a short way of saying "fair enough." What originated as British slang spread on TikTok as a way to acknowledge something as being a valid answer or an understandable result of a situation.

"I remember one time, like, I told a girl I liked her, and she said 'ew'" and I was like 'fairs,'" TikToker @thakiddsam jokingly explained in a June video .

Throughout the weekend, the kids I was with used the saying in conjunction with an OK hand symbol made with the thumb and index finger, in reference to the 👌 emoji. Online, the phrase is sometimes accompanied by AI-generated photos of Wallace from "Wallace and Gromit" using the symbol.

LARPing, or live-action role-playing, might conjure up visions of Dungeons & Dragons costumes and renaissance fairs. But young people are repurposing the word "larping" to call out someone they think is inauthentic.

Going to a fitness class just for the photos is larping being a pilates girl. A summer internship is larping a corporate 9-to-5. Coming into Manhattan from Long Island for the day is larping New York City .

The word is another way to say poser, try-hard or fraud.

"It's someone who is performative in the way that they're dressing or acting or doing something, and it's not actually authentic to who they are as an individual," Morgan Hurlock of Philadelphia previously told USA TODAY. "It's almost like you're calling someone out."

One camper told me that her boyfriend was "huzz," to which a counselor jokingly replied, "you're too young to have a husband!"

Despite how the word sounds, it's not short for marriage, the kids explained. The term refers to a crush or romantic partner. It originally was a derogatory way to refer to a group of women, as a distorted spelling of the word "hoes," but the word has taken on a more general use.

"The typa stuff that only happens to me at school infront of the huzz," one TikTok joked over a compilation of embarrassing moments.

The term was popularized by streamer Kai Cenat around February 2023, according to Merriam-Webster .

If you haven't recognized any of the words on this list yet, you might be Unc.

The word, shorthand for "uncle," is a term for someone perceived as out of touch or old, not unlike "Boomer." The word originated within African American Vernacular English (AAVE) and grew more popular through use in rap and hip hop music, according to Merriam-Webster .

The kids at camp quickly found an obvious candidate for the word in a 50-something-year-old volunteer in our group, who they deemed "camp dad." As they rejoiced in teaching him slang throughout the weekend, it was clear that "unc" could be a term of endearment.

But you don't have to be anywhere near your 50s to start facing the unc allegations, as the cut off seems to be getting younger by the day.

"When I remember my siblings are slowly reaching unc status," 19-year-old TikToker Dasha Sprinkle wrote over an audio about turning 35.

Perhaps the most surprising new slang term I heard that weekend was "fries."

I was familiar with the "Just put the fries in the bag" meme, an online insult that insinuates that the person should stop talking and get back to a fast-food job.

But kids have shortened the phrase to simply saying "fries" as a quick way to tell someone to wrap it up or get to the point.

The slang originated with a 2022 Facebook post from user Andre Jamar Milburn, reading, "I AINT SEEN YOU SINCE HIGHSCHOOL," with his response "JUST PUT THE KETCHUP IN MY BAG BRO 🤣🤣," according to knowyourmeme.com , and eventually went onto incorporate fries instead of ketchup.

Online, the shorthand may be accompanied by the fries and peace sign emoji 🍟✌️.

What does this slang say about young people?

Words like "unc" and "fries" might sound like nonsense, but this slang category reveals the way young people are constantly trying to determine what's "cringe," what's authentic and what's trying too hard. Social slang has existed in every generation, but the virality and speed of the internet have accelerated the way Gen Z and Gen Alpha's slang spreads and evolves.

Much of young people's slang today revolves around social judgement, whether it's the "larping" calling out posers for being performative or "unc" to indicate someone as being out of touch.

"We learn about ourselves and where we stand in the world only from the reactions and responses we get from others," Don Grant, a media psychologist who is the National Adviser of Healthy Device Management for Newport Healthcare, previously told USA TODAY. "For Gen Z and Gen Alpha, that public sphere is online. "They grew up with everything online becoming their social currency and the litmus of who they are."

articles.title: Eleições no Ceará: TRE explica longas filas e demora para votar | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a Justiça Eleitoral, votação para presidente, governador, senador, deputado federal e deputado estadual pode deixar o atendimento mais demorado; eleitores relatam espera em diferentes pontos do estado.
articles.summary: O TRE-CE justifica que as longas filas nas eleições no Ceará ocorrem pelo número de cargos e recomenda o uso da "cola" para agilizar a votação.
articles.body:
Eleitores enfrentam longas filas em diversos locais de votação no Ceará neste domingo (4), dia do primeiro turno das eleições. Há reclamações de demora em diferentes cidades do estado. Segundo o Tribunal Regional Eleitoral do Ceará (TRE-CE), porém, a formação de filas em alguns locais é esperada devido ao número de cargos que precisam ser escolhidos nesta eleição .

De acordo com Lorena Moraes, secretária de Eleições do TRE-CE, os cartórios eleitorais informaram à Justiça Eleitoral sobre a formação de filas em alguns locais. Ela explicou que a votação tende a ser mais lenta por se tratar de uma eleição geral, na qual cada eleitor precisa fazer seis escolhas .

Eleitores formam fila para votar no Ceará — Foto: SVM

Neste domingo, o eleitor cearense vota para:

A votação para o Senado exige dois votos porque duas vagas estão em disputa no estado.

"Estamos em uma eleição geral, com seis cargos. Então, uma eleição que tende naturalmente a ser uma eleição mais lenta", afirmou Lorena.

TRE orienta eleitores a agilizar votação

Segundo a secretária, os mesários são orientados a adotar procedimentos que possam acelerar o atendimento. Um exemplo é a realização de tarefas de forma paralela: enquanto um eleitor está na urna eletrônica, o secretário da seção pode conferir os documentos dos próximos eleitores que aguardam na fila.

O TRE também orienta os eleitores a adotarem algumas medidas para reduzir o tempo de espera.

Uma delas é conferir antecipadamente o local e a seção de votação. Outra recomendação é chegar ao local com um documento de identificação em mãos, facilitando o procedimento de apresentação à mesa receptora.

A Justiça Eleitoral também recomenda que o eleitor leve uma "cola" de papel com os números dos candidatos. A medida ajuda a reduzir o tempo dentro da cabine de votação.

"Levar os seus votos anotados numa cola de papel, para que quando ele entre na cabina de votação ele demore o menor tempo possível dentro da cabina", orientou Lorena.

Para quem ainda não votou, o TRE recomenda, se possível, dar preferência ao período entre 11h e 15h. Segundo Lorena, historicamente esse intervalo registra um fluxo menor de eleitores.

Não há, contudo, um tempo médio definido para cada votação. A duração varia de acordo com cada eleitor.

A secretária explicou que, considerando todas as etapas, são necessários 25 cliques na urna eletrônica, entre a digitação dos números dos candidatos e as confirmações. O tempo pode ser ainda maior caso o eleitor precise corrigir alguma escolha.

TRE registra 72 ocorrências e troca 11 urnas

Além das filas, o TRE-CE também registrou ocorrências relacionadas às urnas eletrônicas ao longo da manhã. Até as 11h deste domingo, eram 72 ocorrências em todo o Ceará, segundo a secretária de Eleições.

Do total, 11 urnas eletrônicas precisaram ser substituídas.

Lorena ressaltou que a Secretaria de Eleições acompanha especificamente as ocorrências relacionadas às urnas. Informações sobre crimes eleitorais, como boca de urna, são acompanhadas por outros setores.

A orientação para quem presenciar alguma irregularidade é procurar as forças policiais presentes nas proximidades dos locais de votação ou registrar a ocorrência pelo aplicativo Pardal. Segundo o TRE, as denúncias registradas pelo aplicativo são encaminhadas ao Ministério Público para averiguação.

articles.title: Zema vota com celular na mão em Araxá | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato à presidência pelo partido Novo votou na Escola Estadual Delfim Moreira, na manhã deste domingo (4). Justiça Eleitoral vai apurar o uso de celular pelo candidato.
articles.summary: Candidato à presidência pelo partido Novo votou na Escola Estadual Delfim Moreira, na manhã deste domingo (4).
articles.body:
O candidato à Presidência da República Romeu Zema (Novo) votou na manhã deste domingo (4) na Escola Estadual Delfim Moreira, no Centro de Araxá , no Alto Paranaíba. Durante a votação, Zema utilizou o celular na cabine da urna eletrônica.

Em entrevista à imprensa, Zema disse que entrou no local com o aparelho por hábito e que não foi alertado previamente.

“Eu ando com o celular o dia todo, né? Ele é quase como se fosse um dedo. Ninguém me lembrou ali e eu fui votar normalmente, mas isso não afetou em nada o meu voto, a minha forma de votar. Não fotografei nada, não fiz nada com o celular ali. Fui só votar mesmo. A colinha estava no papel, levei no papel. Se eu tivesse sido alertado, eu entregava na hora. Acho que nós temos coisas muito mais importantes aí, como essa lá do Paraná, que nós estamos vendo, para estar acompanhando e questionando. Da minha parte, foi até filmado, dá para ver lá que eu não fiz nada com o celular. Bom dia aí para todos.”

Ele chegou ao local por volta das 9h e foi acompanhado por apoiadores. Em um vídeo registrado do candidato, é possível vê-lo olhando para o celular enquanto vota. Também é possível ver outro celular apoiado na mesa da cabine. (Veja acima).

Segundo apuração da TV Integração, a equipe da Justiça Eleitoral que estava na seção não impediu que Zema votasse usando o celular.

O Ministério Público Eleitoral de Minas Gerais estuda a apresentação de uma denúncia contra o candidato Romeu Zema.

O presidente do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de Minas Gerais (TRE-MG), Carlos Henrique Perpétuo Braga, afirmou que a Justiça Eleitoral vai apurar o uso de celular pelo candidato à Presidência Romeu Zema dentro da cabine de votação.

Segundo o magistrado, o uso do aparelho no momento do voto é proibido, e a violação do sigilo da votação pode configurar crime eleitoral. O presidente ressaltou, porém, que eventual responsabilização depende de uma denúncia formal apresentada pelo Ministério Público.

Por meio de nota, o TRE-MG também informou que "todos os mesários foram instruídos acerca da proibição de uso de celular e outros equipamentos que violem o sigilo do voto na cabine de votação, Desse modo, fatos desta natureza que forem registrados serão apurados. A violação do sigilo do voto é crime eleitoral, estabelecido no art. 312 do Código Eleitoral, sujeito a pena de até dois anos de detenção."

Romeu Zema vota com celular na mão em Araxá — Foto: Caio Ranieri/TV Integração

Romeu também afirmou estar confiante na candidatura e disse esperar que os eleitores reconheçam sua trajetória como gestor nos setores privado e público.

“Certeza, nós vamos mostrar que temos eleitores em todos os estados do Brasil, em todas as cidades, pessoas que ainda acreditam numa proposta de mudança de alguém que tem histórico de gestão tanto no setor privado quanto no público”, afirmou.

O candidato também comparou Minas Gerais ao Brasil e disse que os resultados de sua gestão no estado o credenciam para administrar o país.

“E o Brasil é só uma questão de escala, é dez vezes Minas Gerais. E quem faz um bom governo em Minas tem todas as condições de fazer um bom governo no Brasil, já que Minas é quase que uma miniatura do Brasil”, declarou.

Zema ainda afirmou esperar que a democracia seja exercida “na sua plenitude” e criticou uma decisão judicial que, segundo ele, alterou as regras do Debate da Globo que acabou sendo cancelado.

“Fui vítima, na quinta-feira, de uma decisão de última hora, sem pé e sem cabeça, que mudou as regras do debate que acabou sendo cancelado”, disse.

O candidato também criticou a atuação do Judiciário. “Tão lamentável que esse tipo de fato, o Judiciário, que deveria ser um poder moderador, tem sido um poder incendiário que só acentua as crises e intensifica os problemas”, afirmou.

articles.title: Alckmin vota em São Paulo após acompanhar Lula e Haddad em seções eleitorais | G1
articles.standfirst: Na véspera da eleição, Alckmin participou de uma caminhada de campanha ao lado de Lula entre a Avenida Paulista e a Praça Roosevelt.
articles.summary: Na véspera da eleição, Alckmin participou de uma caminhada de campanha ao lado de Lula entre a Avenida Paulista e a Praça Roosevelt.
articles.body:
O vice-presidente da República e candidato à reeleição Geraldo Alckmin (PSB) votou neste domingo (4) no Colégio Santo Américo, no Morumbi, Zona Sul de São Paulo. Ele disputa novamente a Vice-Presidência na chapa encabeçada pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).

Antes de votar, Alckmin acompanhou Lula em seu local de votação, em São Bernardo do Campo, no ABC Paulista, e o candidato ao governo de São Paulo Fernando Haddad (PT), que votou em Indianópolis, na Zona Sul da capital.

Ao chegar à seção eleitoral, Alckmin apresentou um título de eleitor físico antigo. Após votar, afirmou que este é um dia de “ouvir as urnas e o povo” e destacou o significado da votação para a democracia. “O povo decide. Essa é a beleza da democracia”, disse. Ele também classificou o momento como um “ato de amor ao próximo”.

Alckmin afirmou ter “grande confiança” no resultado e disse que as eleições são um momento de comparação entre governos. Segundo o vice-presidente, houve avanços na economia, na saúde e na educação durante o atual mandato. Ele também afirmou que, graças a Lula, “a democracia brasileira foi salva” nos últimos quatro anos.

Questionado sobre as pesquisas eleitorais, Alckmin afirmou que Lula pode vencer no primeiro turno ou disputar um segundo turno, mas ponderou que é preciso aguardar o resultado das urnas.

Alckmin também lembrou que a votação ocorre no Dia de São Francisco de Assis, celebrado em 4 de outubro, e citou o santo como exemplo de humildade e compaixão.

Na véspera da eleição, Alckmin participou de uma caminhada de campanha ao lado de Lula entre a Avenida Paulista e a Praça Roosevelt, na região central de São Paulo. O ato ocorreu no sábado (3), último dia permitido para atividades de campanha nas ruas antes do primeiro turno.

Alckmin foi eleito vice-presidente em 2022, na chapa de Lula. Durante o atual mandato, também comandou o Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços (MDIC).

Antes de chegar à Vice-Presidência, Alckmin construiu sua trajetória política em São Paulo. Foi governador do estado entre 2001 e 2006 e novamente entre 2011 e 2018. Também disputou a Presidência da República em 2006 e 2018, quando ainda era filiado ao PSDB.

Em 2022, após deixar o PSDB e ingressar no PSB, passou a integrar a chapa presidencial de Lula, seu antigo adversário político. Os dois venceram Jair Bolsonaro (PL) no segundo turno daquela eleição.

articles.title: Corpos de adolescentes desaparecidos após afogamento são encontrados | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítimas desapareceram durante passeio de canoa em Feira de Santana. Os corpos foram localizados entre sábado (3) e domingo (4)
articles.summary: Após afogamento no Rio Jacuípe, bombeiros localizam corpos de jovens que desapareceram durante um passeio de canoa em Feira de Santana.
articles.body:
Corpos dos adolescentes desaparecidos após afogamento no Rio Jacuípe são encontrados — Foto: Redes sociais

Dois adolescentes que desapareceram após um afogamento no Rio Jacuípe na sexta-feira (2), em Feira de Santana , segunda maior cidade da Bahia, foram encontrados mortos entre sábado (3) e este domingo (4).

De acordo com o Corpo de Bombeiros, as vítimas já estavam sem vida e em estado iniciado de decomposição quando foram localizadas.

Os corpos foram encontrados depois que começaram a boiar no rio. Equipes de mergulhadores realizavam buscas desde a tarde de sexta-feira, quando os adolescentes desapareceram durante um passeio de canoa.

Os dois adolescentes estavam em uma canoa com outros jovens quando um deles caiu na água. O segundo pulou no rio para tentar ajudá-lo, mas os dois desapareceram.

Os demais adolescentes que estavam na embarcação conseguiram retornar à superfície e pedir ajuda. Pessoas que estavam no local também tentaram localizar as vítimas, mas não conseguiram.

O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado pelo Centro Integrado de Comunicações (Cicom) após testemunhas relatarem o ocorrido. Uma equipe de Feira de Santana iniciou as buscas e, diante da dificuldade para encontrar os adolescentes, mergulhadores de Salvador foram acionados.

articles.title: VÍDEO: drone russo atinge ponte movimentada em Kiev; 2 ficam feridos | G1
articles.standfirst: A Ponte Norte, alvejada neste domingo (4) é uma das mais importantes da capital ucraniana. Ataque ocorreu em meio à visita do chanceler da Alemanha, Friedrich Merz, que se encontrou com o presidente Volodymyr Zelensky.
articles.summary: A Ponte Norte, alvejada neste domingo (4) é uma das mais importantes da capital ucraniana. Ataque ocorreu em meio à visita do chanceler da Alemanha, Friedrich Merz, que se encontrou com o presidente Volodymyr Zelensky.
articles.body:
Um drone russo atingiu uma das principais pontes de Kiev , capital da Ucrânia , neste domingo (4) e duas pessoas ficaram feridas, segundo o prefeito Vitaly Klitschko.

Um vídeo compartilhado nas redes sociais pelo presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky , mostrou que o ataque ocorreu quando a Ponte Norte tinha um grande fluxo de veículos. Veja acima.

"Nesta manhã, os russos atacaram novamente a Ponte Pivnichnyi [Ponte Norte, em português], em Kiev, com um drone. (...) Entre os principais alvos desses terroristas, como sempre, estão edifícios residenciais comuns, infraestrutura crítica — tudo o que faz parte da vida cotidiana normal", afirmou Zelensky.

A Ponte Norte já havia sido atacada no sábado , segundo Zelensky e Klitschko. Já a Ponte Sul, em outro ponto de Kiev, também foi atacada por um drone russo de propulsão à jato na sexta-feira (2), afirmaram as autoridades.

O ataque deste domingo ocorreu em meio à visita do chanceler da Alemanha, Friedrich Merz , a Kiev. Ele chegou à capital ucraniana sob o som de sirenes de ataque aéreo e se encontrou com o Zelensky.

Cratera na Ponte Norte, uma das mais importantes de Kiev, após ataque de drone russo em 4 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Stringer

Merz prometeu neste domingo mais apoio econômico à Ucrânia e pediu que a Rússia interrompa seus ataques contra o território ucraniano, que estão ficando cada vez mais intensos.

“Só posso repetir mais uma vez, deste lugar: senhor Putin, ponha fim a esta guerra sem sentido. Estamos prontos para conversar, estamos prontos para discutir como pôr fim a esta guerra, mas esses ataques bárbaros contra a população civil da Ucrânia precisam parar”, disse o chanceler alemão.

Presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelensky, recebe o chanceler da Alemanha, Friedrich Merz, em Kiev em 4 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Thomas Peter

Quatro alertas de ataque aéreo foram ouvidos em toda a capital na manhã de domingo, e explosões e sistemas de defesa aérea também foram ouvidos em diferentes pontos da cidade.

Durante sua visita a Kiev, Merz e Zelensky concluirão um acordo para a produção conjunta de vários tipos de drones. Os dois líderes visitaram o edifício gravemente danificado da Academia de Ciências da Ucrânia , onde pelo menos duas pessoas morreram em um ataque com drones na semana passada.

articles.title: Eleições em Santarém: Correria na Escola Rio Tapajós na abertura | G1
articles.standfirst: Escola Rio Tapajós concentra cerca de 3 mil votantes neste domingo (4). Município soma mais de 253 mil eleitores aptos e conta com gratuidade no transporte público.
articles.summary: Eleições em Santarém começam com correria na Escola Rio Tapajós, o maior colégio eleitoral da cidade, que conta com transporte gratuito neste domingo.
articles.body:
A abertura dos portões na Escola Estadual Rio Tapajós, considerada o maior colégio eleitoral de Santarém , no oeste do Pará, foi marcada por pressa e correria de eleitores nas primeiras horas da manhã deste domingo (4). Cerca de 3 mil pessoas são esperadas para votar no local ao longo do dia. (veja o vídeo acima).

Registros em vídeo mostram o momento exato em que os portões da instituição foram abertos e dezenas de eleitores se apressaram pelos corredores da escola para garantir lugar na fila antes do início da votação.

Eleitores correram para votar em maior colégio eleitoral de Santarém — Foto: Ulisses Farias/TV Tapajós

Nas imagens é possível ver que assim que os portões da Escola Rio Tapajós são abertos, um grupo de eleitores acelera o passo no corredor de entrada do colégio eleitoral. Homens, mulheres e idosos seguem em direção aos blocos de salas de aula para localizar suas respectivas seções de votação.

O vídeo mostra ainda que em poucos minutos, o fluxo de eleitores toma conta dos corredores internos e as primeiras filas começam a se formar em frente às salas antes da liberação das urnas eletrônicas.

Santarém é o maior colégio eleitoral do oeste paraense, com mais de 253 mil eleitores aptos a votar nas Eleições de 2026 . Ao longo do município, seções eleitorais urbanas e rurais foram preparadas para receber os cidadãos.

Para facilitar o deslocamento e garantir o acesso às seções de votação, o transporte coletivo urbano opera com tarifa zero durante todo o domingo (4). A frota de ônibus circula em esquema normal de dia útil para atender à demanda da população.

articles.title: US Marine arrested on suspicion of murder after 'brutal and heinous' death in Japan
articles.summary: Officials in Japan said they lodged a "strong" protest with the United States.
articles.body:
A U.S. service member was arrested on suspicion of murder and robbery after a Japanese woman's body was discovered in a hotel in Okinawa, local officials said, describing the alleged killing as a "heinous" incident that prompted the Japanese government to lodge a protest with the United States.

Shinjiro Koizumi, the Japanese minister of defense, said a U.S. Marine lance corporal was arrested on Sunday after the woman's body was found early on Saturday in Naha, the capital city of the Okinawa prefecture.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said the Okinawa Prefectural Police were investigating the incident as a murder.

"The occurrence of such an extremely brutal and heinous incident is a matter of profound regret, and as the Government of Japan, we have lodged a strong protest with the U.S. side," she said on social media.

NHK, Japan's public broadcaster, identified the suspect as Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, who was stationed at U.S. Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, a base a few miles outside Naha. The broadcaster identified the alleged victim as Yagi Anna, 39, saying she was pronounced dead at the scene.

U.S. officials did not immediately confirm the identity of the service member who was arrested, nor did they say whether the person had been officially charged in connection with the death.

"We are actively cooperating with Japanese authorities, in response to allegations of serious criminal actions by a Marine assigned to the III Marine Expeditionary Force," the force said in a statement on social media. "We extend our deepest condolences to the victim's family and friends."

Tens of thousands of U.S. troops are stationed across Japan, including in the country's southernmost prefecture, Okinawa, which is home to several U.S. bases.

The U.S. Embassy in Tokyo said it was aware of the incident and was extending "our deepest condolences to the bereaved family of the deceased."

"At present, an investigation is underway to clarify the facts, and the United States Government continues to cooperate closely with the Government of Japan and local authorities," the embassy said in a statement .

George Glass, the U.S. ambassador to Japan, said he had spoken on Sunday morning with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Okinawa's governor, adding that his office was providing full cooperation with an investigation into the death.

articles.title: A North Dakota farm kid turned ag-tech entrepreneur; his company puts real farm maps on children's play rugs
articles.summary: A North Dakota farm kid has turned real agricultural maps into children's play rugs, giving toy tractors and combines a miniature version of the
articles.body: A North Dakota farm kid has turned real agricultural maps into children's play rugs, giving toy tractors and combines a miniature version of the landscapes they come from. Nathan Faleide, founder of Boundri, grew up on a farm in North Dakota and around agricultural mapping through his family's Satshot business. Boundri was started in 2022 and grew from a play rug Faleide made for his children into a company that now puts personalised maps on rugs and other products. Today, Boundri sells mapped play rugs, blankets, wall maps, prints and other customised products, while its mapping background stretches back decades through the Faleide family's work in agricultural technology.From a North Dakota farm to agricultural mappingFaleide's connection to farming began early. On Boundri's current About Us page, he says he grew up on a farm in North Dakota and that farm toys were central to his daily routine. He also says he "did farm a little" himself, but adds that it "wasn't my time." At the same time, he grew up around agricultural mapping through his family's company, Satshot. Faleide says that experience helped develop his expertise in software and maps, eventually providing the technical background behind Boundri.Satshot's history dates to 1994, when Lanny Faleide, Nathan's father, built software to create variable-rate maps using satellite imagery. Satshot says Lanny had more than 20 years of farming experience at the time and that the idea grew from flying as a pilot over his own fields and those of neighbouring farmers in the mid-to-late 1980s. The company also links the development of the technology to difficult conditions in farming during that period. The technology has since continued under Boundri. Satshot's current website describes Satshot as a brand, service and product of Boundri Inc., and says the technology created by Lanny has continued in a new direction with Nathan Faleide. It also says Boundri will continue to run the Satshot brand, product and service "for the time being" while developing new connections and tools around mapping and imagery.How the play-rug idea beganThe first idea was much closer to home. On Boundri's own website, Faleide says the business began with a farm-toy play rug he made for his children. He describes the family as the inspiration for Boundri and says the project grew after seeing the enjoyment his children got from the rug. DTN reported in December 2022 that Faleide had nearly 25 years of experience in precision agriculture and mapping at the time and had long wanted to do more imagery-based art. The publication reported that when he introduced an early prototype, his children began playing with their farm toys on it. A photograph of the rug was subsequently shared by a friend on Twitter, after which orders began arriving. DTN reported that about 230 orders came in while the business was still in its early stages.AgWeb also reported that the product gained attention on Twitter as the business began taking off. An autumn 2022 report from Agweek described Boundri's initial offering as generic farm-print rugs, with custom products expected to follow. The early launch eventually developed into the personalised products that now form a major part of Boundri's range. Rather than limiting the designs to generic farm scenes, the company built its products around maps and imagery connected to specific locations.What Boundri sells todayFarm play rugs remain one of Boundri's main products. Its current site lists personalised farm play rugs in three sizes and also offers custom-upload rugs and other mapped products. The company says its rugs are made from polyester chenille, have hemmed edges and a no-skid polyester backing, and can be cleaned with dish soap, a rag and a hose. It also says the rugs fold for storage and are lightweight. For customers who already have their own imagery, Boundri's FAQ provides more specific instructions. It says satellite, plane or drone images can be uploaded through the company's Custom Product Builder, rather than through its main-page products. The FAQ says the files must currently be JPG or PNG and smaller than 50 MB.Boundri's product page also explains the proof process. Customers can order an item and then send a note explaining any changes they want. The company says a proof is provided before the item is printed. The business now extends beyond children's play rugs. Boundri's website lists blankets, puzzles, onesies, canvas prints and other mapped products, while its wall-map and mural work can include features such as field boundaries, attributes and other map layers. The company says these custom projects are handled on a case-by-case basis.The "carpet farming" ideaThe phrase "carpet farming" appears in both coverage of Boundri and the company's own current website. DTN used the phrase when it covered the business in 2022, while Boundri uses it on its product pages to describe the children who play with its farm rugs. Its current Custom Upload Rugs page, for example, describes the product as a gift for "little carpet farmers."The concept gives children something more specific than a generic farm-themed play surface. Boundri's products can represent actual locations, turning maps associated with farms and other meaningful places into physical objects that can be used, displayed or given as gifts. For Faleide, the business brings together two parts of his background: farming and agricultural mapping. The technology behind Satshot grew from his family's experience with agricultural imagery and mapping, while Boundri has taken that knowledge into a very different kind of product. articles.title: ‘New doctrine’ of strikes: Zelenskyy vows to hit Russian refineries as infrastructure warfare escalates
articles.summary: Ukraine has vowed to step up attacks on Russian oil refineries in response to what president Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as a new Russian strategy of
articles.body: Ukraine has vowed to step up attacks on Russian oil refineries in response to what president Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as a new Russian strategy of targeting infrastructure across Ukrainian cities, including energy, transport and logistics networks.Zelenskyy told Reuters that Ukrainian intelligence had obtained documents indicating that Russian president Vladimir Putin had approved a broader range of targets ahead of the winter campaign, including infrastructure, roads, schools and hospitals. He said the aim was to disrupt daily life and pressure people to leave Kyiv and other cities.“We have to respond in any way we can. With their attacks on our energy, we have to respond on their energy. First of all, oil refiners etc: what gives money to them for this war,” Zelenskyy said.He said Ukraine would respond against Russian energy infrastructure but would not deliberately target civilian facilities.From energy grids to bridgesThe shift comes as Russian attacks on Kyiv have increasingly focused on infrastructure that keeps the capital functioning.Over the past week, Russian drones and missiles have struck energy and telecommunications assets as well as road and rail infrastructure. Russia has also targeted bridges over the Dnipro River connecting eastern and western Kyiv, marking a new pressure point on the city's transport network.The attacks point to a broader form of infrastructure-based warfare in which the objective is not only to destroy military positions, but to disrupt the systems that allow a city to function: electricity, communications, transport, logistics and supply routes.Moscow says its strikes are retaliatory responses to Ukrainian attacks on Russian territory. Both sides deny deliberately targeting civilians.Zelenskyy, however, said Ukrainian intelligence documents showed the Russian objective was to make life in Ukrainian cities increasingly difficult.“They allow them to attack infrastructure, logistics, and especially to attack in the cities, in the villages, everywhere, roads, schools, hospitals,” he told Reuters. “To pressure people to leave the capital, leave different cities: this is the goal of the operation.”Ukraine’s answer: hit what funds Russia’s warZelenskyy said Ukraine's response would focus on Russian energy infrastructure, particularly oil refineries that generate revenue for Moscow's war effort.The strategy also reflects Kyiv's broader campaign against Russia's energy sector. Ukraine has repeatedly targeted Russian oil facilities in an effort to disrupt fuel production and export revenues, although US president Donald Trump has urged Zelenskyy to stop striking Russian oil installations, arguing that the attacks were contributing to higher global diesel prices.Zelenskyy said he had seen no indication that Moscow was ready to resume meaningful negotiations or agree to a ceasefire covering energy infrastructure.The infrastructure fight comes as Ukraine prepares for another winter in which Russian attacks are expected to focus heavily on electricity and water systems.Ukrainian officials say Russia has stockpiled hundreds of ballistic missiles ahead of a new campaign. Last winter, Russian strikes repeatedly damaged energy infrastructure, leaving parts of the country without electricity and heating for extended periods.Russia has also expanded its use of faster jet-powered Shahed drones, which Ukrainian air defences have struggled to intercept. Zelenskyy said Ukraine was relying heavily on F-16 and MiG fighter aircraft to destroy them, but ammunition supplies for the aircraft were running low.Kyiv is therefore working on cheaper alternatives, including electronic jamming and new interceptor drones. Zelenskyy said two models had been tested but were achieving a success rate of only around 30% so far.The infrastructure campaign is unfolding alongside fighting over territory in eastern Ukraine. Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces had recaptured around 140 sq km of Donbas in a counteroffensive code-named “Vivaldi”, while Russia continues to demand control of the entire Donbas as a condition for any peace agreement.You use AI every day. articles.title: New Zealand farmer lost more than half his asparagus crop to storms; he turned the damaged spears into an award-winning freeze-dried snack
articles.summary: A wet, cold, and windy October left one Canterbury asparagus grower facing a devastating season, with more than half of his crop lost to severe weather.
articles.body: A wet, cold, and windy October left one Canterbury asparagus grower facing a devastating season, with more than half of his crop lost to severe weather. Instead of accepting the damage, Dave Marsh of Ashburton, New Zealand, turned the misshapen and unsellable spears into a freeze-dried snack that has already earned three silver awards at the New Zealand Artisan Food Awards. His story shows how a farmer under pressure from rising costs can find fresh value in produce that shops would never stock. This article explains what went wrong in the fields, how the snack came about, and why the idea matters for growers wanting less waste.How the weather destroyed four of seven hectares of asparagus in CanterburyHarvest was well underway when October turned difficult for Marsh. The month began wet and cold, and the winds that followed were, in his words, horrendous. The storms left four of his seven hectares ruined, because the spears had grown twisted and bent and could not be sold. Marsh had to cut everything back, which cost him roughly a week of production.Why rejected asparagus spears had no commercial value in shops but plenty of potential as a snackEven in a good season, a share of every asparagus harvest never reaches the shelf. Marsh told 1News that spears can be damaged on the processing belt and lose their tips, while others are simply too short, too fat, too bent, or too seedy. With overheads and production costs climbing, he had already been thinking about doing something new with this unsold produce. The bad weather made that search more urgent.Inside the freeze-dried asparagus snack, uncooked product that keeps the nutrients intactThe result is a freeze-dried asparagus snack sold under the My Farm Fresh brand. Marsh describes it as a healthy, uncooked, completely natural product that retains the nutrients asparagus is known for. It also gives his farm something different to offer, which is valuable when the fresh crop is under pressure.Three silver awards at the New Zealand Artisan Food AwardsThe snack has done more than survive its first season. Marsh has taken it to market and won three silver awards at the New Zealand Artisan Food Awards. His experience suggests that produce rejected for its looks can still earn a place in the market when it is given a second life, and that a disastrous growing season can sometimes push a farmer toward a better idea.You use AI every day. articles.title: After Hurricane Katrina, Sandra Bullock helped rebuild a New Orleans school; in 2010, she helped fund its $700,000 medical and dental clinic, designed to provide free healthcare to students
articles.summary: Sandra Bullock has an Academy Award, a Golden Globe and, in 2010 and again in 2014, was ranked as the highest-paid actress in the world.
articles.body: Sandra Bullock has an Academy Award, a Golden Globe and, in 2010 and again in 2014, was ranked as the highest-paid actress in the world. Ask her where her money did the most good, and the answer is not a film deal.It is a flooded high school in New Orleans. Bullock has backed Warren Easton Charter High School since 2006, months after Hurricane Katrina shut its doors. It was one of the best investments she ever made. No wonder she was an honorary member of the Warren Easton Hall of Fame in 2009. She had every right to be there. Her efforts in rebuilding the school post-Katrina were notable.The flood closed the school doorsKatrina closed the school's building and left about $4 million in damage. In Mid-City, Warren Easton, one of the oldest public high schools in Louisiana, was on the verge of shutting down. Local officials considered closing it. Alumni, students and faculty raised private funds to reopen it as a charter school.Sandra Bullock had a personal connection with New Orleans. Her adopted son was born in the city, and so she hoped to rescue the school. The slow response from the government also made her help necessary.The giving came in pieces: band uniforms, athletic lockers, college scholarships, leadership seminars, audio and video equipment, and part of the bill for a renovated auditorium, according to the Allstate Sugar Bowl committee that honoured her in 2010. Her total contribution has never been made public. ‘My contributions to Warren Easton are the best investments I’ve ever made,’ Bullock later said.‘I just write the checks,’ the actress said in 2009. She also lent her name. Ahead of The Blind Side's release, she and Warner Bros. hosted a New Orleans premiere to raise money for the school.Without Bullock, the recovery would not have been this fast, Easton's principal, Alexina Medley, told the Associated Press. ‘We would not have returned as soon as we did. She's come to our rescue several times, and in a pinch, she's definitely helped us out.’Sandra Bullock opens a health clinic in New OrleansIn August 2010, during the fifth anniversary of Katrina's landfall, Sandra Bullock's efforts helped open a health clinic in New Orleans. The $700,000 medical and dental clinic received major funding from the Kellogg Foundation, the San Francisco 49ers Foundation and Bullock, though it is unclear how much of it was hers. As always, she chose to keep her contributions private. The clinic was intended to bring healthcare services to students in a part of the city that had struggled to regain access to doctors and dentists after the hurricane. Those without insurance were among the beneficiaries of the programme.Bullock steered the day towards celebration, acknowledging the date could be hard for some. ‘We're here to celebrate an anniversary and though that might be hard for some, I choose to emphasise the word 'celebrate'. Sometimes tragedies bring out the very best in people and it's one of the reasons why we stand in this school of excellence today,’ Bullock told the hundreds of attendees gathered in the auditorium. The clinic opened in autumn and provided services ranging from flu shots to emergency care. The community was in urgent need of such a clinic. ‘It will definitely help those students who don't have insurance. I think there should be these types of facilities in all the schools,’ Janell Batiste, who had a daughter at Easton, said at the time.The clinic was only an entry in a long ledger. In 2012, Bullock gave $25,000 to the school. In January 2013, the People's Choice Awards named her its first Favorite Humanitarian, citing her commitment to Easton. In 2014, when she spoke at the school's commencement, she pledged to match donations to the Hall of Fame scholarship campaign for graduating seniors. ‘Every time they walk under that roof, they know they're cared for,’ she told the students. Bullock’s commitment to the school didn’t end there. In 2018, the actress participated in a fundraiser for the school. In addition to making a $5,000 personal donation, she said she would match the next $50,000 raised.‘I will match the next 50 thousand dollars! Let’s take care of our future!’ she wrote on the fundraising page. Sandra Bullock made the donation in honour of her late mother, Helga, a German opera singer who died in 2000. In 2020, WGNO named her among the major donors behind $120,000 in scholarships for 41 students. Her contributions to the welfare of the school continue.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Iran tells US there is no military solution to Middle East war
articles.summary: Iran's top diplomat insisted on Sunday that there would be no military solution to the United States' war against the Islamic republic, with talks on ending...
articles.body:
Iran's top diplomat insisted on Sunday that there would be no military solution to the United States' war against the Islamic republic, with talks on ending the conflict apparently at an impasse.

A campaign of heavy bombardment failed to bring a decisive close to the war launched by the US and Israel in late February, and Washington in recent weeks has dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure.

The main point of contention remains Iran's attempt to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, a vital conduit for Gulf oil and gas where a UK maritime agency reported on Sunday another tanker struck by an unknown projectile.

"If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force," Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said at a gathering of foreign ambassadors.

"There is no military solution, nor any solution based on new sanctions," he continued, adding "only negotiations based on justice and fairness" could end the conflict.

The two sides agreed a memorandum of understanding in June that spelled out a framework for a permanent resolution, but Iranian attacks on vessels in the Hormuz prompted a return to US military operations.

Iran has sought to impose its control over the vital shipping lane since the start of the war, striking vessels that attempt to transit without its authorisation.

The US has imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports, and has also struck vessels it accuses of violating it.

On Sunday, the British maritime security agency UKMTO said a tanker in the Hormuz "reported being struck by an unknown projectile, causing damage to the engine room", though the crew were reported safe and no environmental impact was recorded.

The agency did not specify the date of the incident, the vessel's origin or destination, or whether it was an oil tanker or LNG carrier.

Iranian and US officials last week held indirect talks on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, with Tehran saying it presented seven conditions for reopening the strait.

Iran has demanded, among other things, a ceasefire across the Middle East, the unfreezing of its assets abroad, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector and an end to the US naval blockade.

Trump, however, rejected the proposal, while leaving the door open both to further talks or renewed military operations.

Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei on Sunday characterised the latest US counterproposal as being "in line with their previous proposals concerning nuclear issues".

"We have clearly indicated that we are focusing on the issue of the Strait of Hormuz," he said, adding that reopening the waterway required "an end to the disruptions to Iranian commercial maritime traffic and the lifting of sanctions".

The United States and Israel have characterised the war as being necessary to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons -- a goal it has long denied pursuing -- though the focus soon shifted to reopening the Hormuz after its closure sent shockwaves through world energy markets.

The United States has not struck Iran since September 1, but it has recently pursued a fresh military buildup in the region.

US media outlet Axios reported that Washington has deployed additional Patriot missile batteries to Saudi Arabia and Qatar to help protect key energy facilities from possible Iranian retaliation.

It also reported that the USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier and its strike group were heading to the Middle East, where they could join two other US carrier strike groups already in the region.

Axios reported that top Trump cabinet members met Friday to discuss the war in Iran, as well as the conflict in Yemen, where the Tehran-backed Houthis have been fighting government forces and attacking Saudi Arabia.

articles.title: Expelled, suspended or made to write ‘reflection papers’: How Cornell punished 7 men for sexual assault
articles.summary: At Cornell University, disciplinary action against seven fraternity members accused of sexual misconduct ranged from expulsion and suspension to a
articles.body: At Cornell University, disciplinary action against seven fraternity members accused of sexual misconduct ranged from expulsion and suspension to a requirement that some of the men study sexual harassment and write “reflection papers” on their conduct, according to disciplinary records obtained by the New York Times.Two men were expelled, two were suspended and three received lesser sanctions after a Title IX panel reviewed the allegations. The punishments have since drawn scrutiny, including over how Cornell decided what each man was responsible for and what forms of accountability were considered appropriate.The case has also sparked controversy over a claim in Jane Doe’s lawsuit that the accused men were given an opportunity to mitigate their conduct by submitting essays to Cornell. The university has said that description was inaccurate. The disciplinary records show, however, that some of the men were required to write reflection papers as part of their sanctions.None of the seven men has been criminally charged. All have denied wrongdoing, while Cornell's Chi Phi fraternity has been banned from campus. Tompkins County district attorney Matthew Van Houten had declined to prosecute the case in 2024.How Cornell punished the 7The NYT reported that Matthew Ingalls and Jonathan Newell were expelled.The panel found Ingalls responsible for sexual assault and concluded that he had manipulated, exploited and endangered Jane Doe for his own interests and the entertainment of others. Newell had been accused of sexual assault and of encouraging other fraternity members to enter a bedroom where Jane Doe was undressed through a Snapchat message.Winston Lee and Gillio Lopes were suspended. Lee received a two-year suspension followed by disciplinary probation, while Lopes was suspended for three semesters and placed on two years of probation. Both were also ordered not to contact Jane Doe and required to complete sexual-harassment training and write reflection papers.Diego Sarabia, who had already graduated, was declared persona non grata and barred from Cornell's campus for three years. Jane Doe had accused him of forcibly kissing her.Scott Norris and Scott Kretzschmar received lighter sanctions. They were ordered not to contact Jane Doe and to complete training on sexual harassment, social-media use and bystander intervention, as well as write reflection papers.Kretzschmar was not found responsible for sexual assault. A recently unsealed lawsuit showed that Cornell instead found him responsible for a lesser offence of attempted sexual exploitation. His lawyer said he had never been accused of or found responsible for rape and was not present during sexual activity.What happened at the fraternity houseJane Doe originally went to the Chi Phi house at about 11pm on October 19, 2024 to visit Ingalls after spending the evening drinking at a bar, according to the records reviewed by NYT.She told investigators that her intoxication level was around 5 out of 10 when she arrived. After she got there, Ingalls asked whether she wanted a threesome with Newell. She said the men gave her ketamine and alcohol and that, as the night continued, other men engaged in sex acts with her without her consent while she was incapacitated.The disciplinary records show that Newell had sent a Snapchat message encouraging other fraternity members to enter the bedroom while Jane Doe was undressed. She later told police that he had struck her during intercourse hard enough to leave bruises and had manipulated her into ingesting ketamine.Jane Doe's lawyer, Thomas Giuffra, said the sanctions did not reflect the severity of the allegations. Lawyers for some of the men disputed the characterisation of their clients' conduct, while Cornell declined to comment because of federal student-privacy laws.The university's disciplinary findings are separate from the criminal investigation.After Jane Doe's lawsuit became public in September, New York governor Kathy Hochul ordered an independent review of Cornell's handling of the case. She later appointed state Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor with the power to bring criminal charges, according to the NYT.The new disciplinary summaries therefore offer the first detailed public account of how Cornell apportioned responsibility among the seven men, even as questions remain over whether any of the conduct will ultimately result in criminal charges.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'What has changed in 17 years?': Rahul Gandhi hits out at BJP over Bihar flood crisis
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Saturday targeted the BJP-led government over Bihar’s recurring flood
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Saturday targeted the BJP-led government over Bihar’s recurring flood crisis, asking what had changed on the ground in the last 17 years and calling for a permanent solution instead of yearly relief and assurances.In a post on X, while offering his condolences Rahul said that floods had once again struck Bihar with “devastating force”, affecting millions, submerging hundreds of villages and leaving several people dead or missing.“The most heartbreaking thing is that this crisis in Bihar is not new,” Rahul said, pointing to the recurring cycle of floods, deaths, shattered families and migration.“The BJP's double-engine government should tell us — what has it done in the last 17 years to address this annual tragedy? What has changed on the ground?” he asked.Rahul said people in Bihar did not need relief and assurances every year but a permanent solution to the recurring floods.Nearly 50 lakh affectedThe latest flood spell affected 49.67 lakh people across 15 districts, according to the Bihar disaster management department. The affected districts included Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnea, Madhepura and Araria.The floods came amid heavy rainfall in Bihar and neighbouring areas, with officials saying water levels in the Ganga, Sone and Gandak rose sharply after heavy rain in Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh, as well as rainfall in the catchment areas of rivers originating in Nepal.This year's flooding also differed from the usual pattern. While the Kosi and Gandak were responsible for the first two flood spells, the prolonged third spell in September was mainly driven by the swollen Ganga, Sone and Punpun rivers.Government pushes relief, long-term measuresThe Bihar government has stepped up relief operations, with chief minister Samrat Choudhary saying the administration would ensure assistance reached affected families. The state also transferred Rs 579 crore to 8.27 lakh flood-affected families across 15 districts, with each eligible family receiving Rs 7,000.Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan also visited flood-hit areas and assured Bihar of the Centre's support for rescue, relief and rehabilitation. He said the scale of damage and the state's requirements would be placed before Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah.The state government has also been looking beyond immediate relief. Choudhary later said surveys of the Kosi and Mahananda rivers were being conducted as part of a comprehensive study of recurring floods and efforts towards a permanent solution.The issue of embankments has also remained central to the flood response. Bihar's water resources department said scientifically strengthened embankments had remained intact this season, while older ring and zamindari bunds had suffered breaches.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Moscow vows to step up strikes on Ukraine as Zelenskyy threatens to attack more Russian refineries
articles.summary: Russia will intensify strikes on Kyiv and other regions of Ukraine following recent remarks by president Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the Russian defence ministry
articles.body: Russia will intensify strikes on Kyiv and other regions of Ukraine following recent remarks by president Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the Russian defence ministry said on Sunday. The remarks came as Moscow warned of a further escalation in the aerial war after Kyiv threatened to expand attacks on Russian oil refineries.The ministry, cited by Russia's state-run TASS news agency, said that the Russian forces would step up attacks on military facilities, defence industry sites and related infrastructure in Kyiv and elsewhere in Ukraine.The warning followed remarks by Zelenskiy to Reuters that Ukraine would "double down" on attacks against Russian oil refineries in response to what he described as a new Russian campaign targeting infrastructure across Ukrainian cities.Zelenskyy said Ukrainian intelligence had obtained documents indicating that Russian president Vladimir Putin had approved a broader range of targets ahead of the winter campaign."We saw documents and we know that they allow them to attack infrastructure, logistics, and especially to attack in the cities, in the villages, everywhere, roads, schools, hospitals," Zelenskyy told Reuters."To pressure people to leave the capital, leave different cities: this is the goal of the operation," he said.Zelenskiy said Ukraine would respond by targeting Russian energy infrastructure but would not deliberately attack civilian facilities."We have to respond in any way we can. With their attacks on our energy, we have to respond on their energy. First of all, oil refiners etc: what gives money to them for this war," he said."But we will not respond, of course, just like them, on any civilian objects."The latest warning came as attacks on energy, transport and communications infrastructure intensified. Russian drones and missiles have struck targets across Ukraine, while Kyiv has increasingly targeted Russia's oil industry, which it says helps finance Moscow's war effort.On Sunday, a fire broke out at an industrial site in Russia's Krasnodar region after falling drone debris struck the facility in the Temryuk district, regional authorities said. Three people were injured and taken for medical treatment.Meanwhile, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Kyiv on Sunday in a show of support for Ukraine. Merz said Germany would continue backing Kyiv and warned of the wider consequences of Russia's war."If Russia is not stopped, sooner or later its war machine will turn against us," Merz said. "You can continue to count on our help."Zelenskiy thanked Germany on X, saying the two countries would make "important agreements" to strengthen Ukraine's defences. "Russia must be stopped together," he wrote.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: South Carolina birthday girls’ trip allegedly turns deadly at the hands of bartender, friend says
articles.summary: Ruth Peterson said she watched her best friend get shoved down stairs at Coot's Bar & Grill on Edisto Island, South Carolina, during a birthday getaway.
articles.body: A long-awaited getaway for two best friends celebrating birthdays together ended in tragedy when a bartender allegedly shoved a woman down stairs, leaving her fatally injured outside a South Carolina beachside bar. Mary Lopez Hunt, 68, has been charged with voluntary manslaughter and assault and battery of a high and aggravated nature, according to Colleton County court records. Ruth Peterson recalled the painful memory to Fox News Digital on Oct. 1, 2026, just two days before the one-year mark of her friend’s death. Peterson had just left to get their car, as her friend, 62-year-old Minnesota resident Joyce Tomlinson, went to settle their tab at Coot’s Bar & Grill on Edisto Island at about 11 p.m. on Oct. 3, 2025. SEND US A TIP Hearing her friend’s voice, Peterson turned at the bottom of the stairs and looked up, she said. At the top of the stairs, she saw Tomlinson — a woman she described as meek and friendly — exchange words briefly with another woman behind her. She couldn’t hear what was said. "Next thing I know, Joyce had turned around to head back down [the stairs], and this woman runs at her, and with both hands just pushes her, and she just sailed," Peterson said, stifling tears. "She didn't fall down the steps. She didn't roll down the steps… She didn't touch the steps." "She went head first and landed on this concrete slab." Peterson rushed to her friend and couldn’t find a pulse, she said. Tomlinson began bleeding from her mouth and ears, she said. "I knew it was bad." Hunt told authorities that Tomlinson was belligerent and yelled at bartenders before she was asked to leave, records show. She alleges that Tomlinson fell down the stairs. Authorities arrived at the bar and found Tomlinson lying on the pavement at the bottom of the stairs, according to a heavily redacted report. GOT A TIP? Tomlinson was flown to a hospital by helicopter and she died a little more than three weeks later. ‘Itty-bitty, tiny woman’ Tomlinson was an "itty-bitty, tiny" woman with a "meek and mild" personality, Peterson said. She can’t believe the legal aide who helped people resolve financial issues would start a fight, she said. Tomlinson and Peterson had been friends for 50 years, Peterson said. As young girls in Minnesota, they loved to roller skate together. And as they grew older and started families of their own, their children grew up playing together, too. Eventually, they moved away from each other but remained close friends. For years, they’d discussed meeting to celebrate their 60th birthdays together. But "life got in the way," Peterson said. Then in 2025, Tomlinson called and said she was coming to visit in October so they could celebrate their birthdays together, Peterson remembered. When they checked into their rented condo in Edisto Beach, South Carolina, an employee recommended Coot’s Bar & Grill, she said. They sat at the bar and each had two drinks, Peterson said. When a solo performer began playing music, the two women stood up and danced. Then the bar became crowded, so they decided to leave and catch up at the condo, Peterson said. GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL Tomlinson went to pay the bill. Peterson went for the car. "I left the bar and walked down the steps, the same steps that we came up [to go] in. I turned around to see how far behind me she was… and that's when I saw her standing at the top of the steps." Moments later, her friend was unconscious. They never spoke again. ‘Loving mom,’ ’trustworthy friend’ Tomlinson’s friends and family still are trying to piece together how the fight could turned violent so quickly, Peterson said. At her funeral, friends and family remembered Tomlinson as "a loving mom" and "a trustworthy friend," Peterson wrote in a eulogy read at the funeral. She wasn’t married but did leave behind a son. "It's just been very surreal," Peterson said. "It's very hard to believe that she's gone and that somebody would do that to another person." Hunt was released on $100,000 bond for each of her charges. Later, bond was revoked and she was taken back into custody in the Colleton County Jail in Walterboro, South Carolina. It was not immediately clear why her bond was revoked. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital reached out to Coot’s Bar & Grill for comment. Hunt's attorney could not be reached.

articles.title: Did Israel ignore warnings? UAE shared info about flydubai crew & Omani co-pilot before flight
articles.summary: The United Arab Emirates had shared with Israel information on the passengers and crew aboard the FlyDubai flight whose Omani co-pilot allegedly attacked
articles.body: The United Arab Emirates had shared with Israel information on the passengers and crew aboard the FlyDubai flight whose Omani co-pilot allegedly attacked the captain and tried to seize control of the aircraft, according to regional officials cited by The Associated Press. The disclosure has raised fresh questions over how the co-pilot was able to board an Israel-bound flight despite having previously been barred from flying by Oman over concerns about his extremist views.The UAE, which is leading the investigation, has described Wednesday's incident as a “terrorist attack”. The co-pilot allegedly attacked Captain Smit Machchhar with the cockpit's crash axe before attempting to take control of the plunging aircraft. The plane, carrying 182 people, was eventually stabilised after the injured captain managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and others to overpower the attacker.Also read: Crew of flydubai demanded release of co-pilot after he attacked Smit, claim flyersThe latest details have put the spotlight on possible security failures in Israel, the UAE and the airlines involved. According to regional officials cited by AP, the UAE had provided Israel with information about those aboard the flight, including their nationalities. Israel, however, had not raised any red flags over either a passenger or crew member, the officials said. Israel's security system under scrutinyThe Shin Bet, Israel's domestic security agency, has said responsibility for vetting passenger lists from foreign flights lies with the transportation ministry. Transportation minister Miri Regev, however, told public broadcaster Kan that security agencies were responsible for flight security and that her ministry had not been given a passenger list or any warning about the co-pilot.Also read: Co-pilot's chilling admission after trying to crash flydubai jetThe Times of Israel, citing Army Radio and internal National Security Council documents, reported that Israeli security bodies had warned for years that the Transportation Ministry was not adequately equipped to carry out security checks on foreign airlines flying into the country.In 2021, Israel's security cabinet removed responsibility for such checks from the Shin Bet and assigned the Civil Aviation Authority, under the transportation ministry, responsibility for ensuring that security procedures on foreign flights met international requirements.A classified 2024 state comptroller report reportedly found that the ministry was not meeting its obligations. In May 2024, the security cabinet ordered the National Security Council to form a team involving the Transportation Ministry, Civil Aviation Authority, Shin Bet, Mossad and Finance Ministry to examine the security framework for international commercial flights.The discussions continued for about a year. According to documents cited by Army Radio, the Shin Bet said it lacked the manpower and budget to handle security checks for foreign flights, while the NSC agreed that the Transportation Ministry should assume responsibility but said it would need additional resources.There was reportedly strong internal opposition within the ministry. One source involved in the discussions told Army Radio: “The Shin Bet and Mossad knew full well that the Transportation Ministry was in pieces, that it had no people, no positions, and no capabilities.”The source added: “How did they just shrug off responsibility like that and dump everything on the transportation ministry? The responsibility lies with the transportation ministry — but the Shin Bet and Mossad also enabled this failure, and the writing was on the wall.”The transportation ministry has rejected the allegations as “completely false”. It said responsibility for foreign flights had existed within the ministry for decades and that it was incorrect to portray it as a recently transferred responsibility. It also said the National Security Council and other security bodies had approved its procedures. Co-pilot was previously barred from flyingThe scrutiny is particularly sharp because the co-pilot, identified by people familiar with the investigation as Hamam al-Hammami, had reportedly already come to the attention of authorities in Oman.According to AP, a regional official and another person familiar with the matter said Oman had barred al-Hammami from flying because of concerns that he had adopted extremist views. He was subsequently moved to an administrative position at Oman Air before later being hired by UAE-based FlyDubai.A Gulf diplomat cited by AP said al-Hammami had undergone standard security checks before being hired, but those checks appeared to focus on criminal convictions rather than examining his background for possible signs of radicalisation.The incident has also raised questions over how an Omani national was permitted to serve on a flight carrying Israeli passengers. Israel and Oman do not have diplomatic relations, and Israel has said it has agreements with foreign airlines restricting pilots from countries without diplomatic ties from operating flights to the country.The UAE has shared information about the incident with Israel as the investigation continues. Four regional countries are reportedly working to establish the co-pilot's motive, with assistance from the US and other Western governments. Investigators have so far not found a connection between him and a militant group, according to a Gulf diplomat cited by AP.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union minister Chirag Paswan on Sunday praised Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi for launching a digital platform named "Satyagraha" to gather information on various issue-based protests occurring across the country.The Union minister said that as many platforms as possible must be provided for the youth to express their views."That is a good thing. I have always advocated for providing as many platforms as possible for the youth and for our Indian citizens to express their views," Paswan said."It was with that very mindset that Rahul Gandhi initiated the Satyagraha," he added.He, however, also targeted the opposition and accused it of spreading lies and raising issues only to abandon them halfway."The name is well-chosen, but the opposition has developed a habit of repeatedly spreading lies and confusion. Raising issues only to abandon them halfway, spreading confusion among the public about everything from EVMs to the SIR," he said."The reality is that the people are rejecting you; you won't grasp this through Satyagraha, but rather through introspection," he added.This comes a day after Rahul launched the "Satyagraha" website and said that protesters can submit details about their causes, find similar movements across the country through an interactive map and seek direct support.“People across the country are fighting for their rights and often fighting alone. Gen Z, students, farmers, tribals, Dalits, women - every struggle has its own story. But the voice that rises alone often gets suppressed. ‘Satyagraha’ is an initiative to bring these voices together on a map. Bapu taught us this; truth is the greatest weapon. But an even greater weapon is standing together with truth in unity. If you’re also fighting against any injustice, share your story. articles.title: 'US has deliberately become a lonelier power': EAM Jaishankar on shifting world order
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday said the global landscape was being shaped by a “radical repositioning” of the United States
articles.body: NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday said the global landscape was being shaped by a “radical repositioning” of the United States and the rise of China, while asserting that India has the potential to move rapidly up the global power hierarchy in the coming years.Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, Jaishankar said the US had “deliberately become a lonelier power” as part of a chosen change in its posture.“No one in the room would disagree with the fact that the landscape today is primarily marked by a radical repositioning of the United States. A repositioning which is a posture of choice and, in a way, it has deliberately become a lonelier power,” Jaishankar said.He identified the rise of China as the second major feature of the changing global order, pointing to the increasingly sharp competition between the two powers.“That competition today, not limited to these two countries, has led to a weaponization of any leverage that any country has. And that competition coexists with the complexity of interdependence,” he said.On India’s prospects, Jaishankar said the country had “decades of high growth” ahead and a demographic profile capable of supporting that growth. He also said India may not have to follow the traditional industrialisation path taken by earlier economies.“I would even argue, a world that is much more creative, where many new possibilities are there, so that we don't necessarily have to tread the earlier path of industrialization,” he said.“The orthodox path will have to devise something much more contemporary for what awaits us,” he added.Jaishankar said countries currently classified as middle powers could follow different trajectories as the global order evolves.“Among the middle powers, some will peel off, some will stay put, some may drop down a bit,” he said.“That is the reality. That will be part of the evolution of the global order,” Jaishankar added.The Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi is being held on October 4 and 5, bringing together senior decision-makers and experts to discuss international security and foreign policy issues.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Sunday lashed out at DMK and its president M K Stalin over escalating personal attacks, while issuing a “stern warning” against derogatory remarks targeting women.Referring to recent political speeches targeting women leaders, Vijay said, “I told you earlier if you vote for the DMK and certain others, it amounts to endorsing those who speak obscenely about women and humiliate them in public spaces. I didn't say that just to score political points. Look at what happened the day before yesterday”.He was referring to alleged controversial remarks by M K Stalin against TVK’s Dharapuram bypoll candidate P Sathyabama while addressing a campaign meeting. Vijay and other TVK leaders have alleged that Stalin's comments amounted to body-shaming the woman candidate.“What kind of vile speech did he (Stalin) make against our sister, Sathyabama. It was so vulgar that one cannot even bear to listen to it. And is he the only one speaking like this. Every single person he has nurtured and brought up is delivering the exact same cheap rhetoric,” Vijay said.“Speak whatever you want about me. I will take it. But if you dare speak against our sister, or against the mothers, sisters, and daughters of our households, I will not stay quiet. This marks a return to the era of MGR,” he added, referring to late Tamil Nadu chief minister and AIADMK founder M G Ramachandran.Vijay made the remarks during a roadshow in bypoll-bound Dharapuram in Tiruppur district, where he campaigned for TVK candidate P Sathyabama ahead of the October 6 assembly bypoll.Vijay began the roadshow around 1 pm in his customised caravan and was expected to cover a 40-km stretch, with the campaign ending at 6 pm.He interacted with voters along the route and briefly travelled on a bullock cart. At several places, people gathered along the roads to greet him, showered flower petals and presented him with flowers, garlands and party towels.Vijay also offered prayers at the Moolanur Vanjiamman shrine, where he was accorded traditional temple honours. At another location, he walked for a short distance, waving to supporters and canvassing votes.The campaign route covered more than 20 public-contact points, including Periyar statue junction, Five Roads junction, Meenakshipuram, Kulathupalayam and Karaiyur. He said he was raising the issue as a “son and brother” of the women of Tamil Nadu.Meanwhile, TVK general secretary (election management) and minister Aadhav Arjuna warned that legal action would be taken against former chief minister M K Stalin and leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin if they continued making derogatory comments against women.Polling in the Dharapuram and Madurantakam constituencies will be held on October 6, while counting of votes is scheduled for October 9.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
